articles.title: CONEXPO-CON/AGG 2026 recap

paras.en: CONEXPO-CON/AGG 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada, reaffirmed its position as the largest construction trade show in North America, drawing more than 140,000 construction professionals from 128 countries across the globe. For Carlisle Brake & Friction, a CentroMotion brand, the week was an incredible opportunity to showcase innovation, strengthen partnerships and gain valuable insights into the future of the construction, mining and aggregate industries. Throughout the busy week, attendees had the chance to speak with our experts and watch live demonstrations of our brake systems, along with our advanced brake and transmission friction solutions for the construction industry.

articles.title: New Facility Brings Off-Highway Wet Friction Production to India

paras.en: New Facility Brings Off-Highway Wet Friction Production to India

Carlisle Brake & Friction has broken ground to expand its Chennai, India manufacturing operations in one of the world’s fastest-growing industrial regions. Having produced mechatronic products in the region for more than 15 years, Carlisle CBF will relocate to add production at a larger site for off-highway paper wet friction discs and steel separator plates. The new facility is scheduled to open in 2027.

The move to expanded space is designed to accommodate manufacturing capabilities needed to serve the growing demand across the agriculture, construction and especially mining industries in India and Southeast Asia. Local production will improve supply chain responsiveness while supporting original equipment and aftermarket requirements in cost-sensitive markets.

Carlisle Brake & Friction is establishing a state-of-the-art wet friction manufacturing facility on par with proven global manufacturing processes in the new Chennai plant, to build a more resilient regional platform. This expansion strengthens our ability to deliver durable wet friction products that help keep critical off-highway equipment productive.

articles.title: Caliber Auto Glass Acquires Arrow Auto Glass, Expands into Four States
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: Caliber Auto Glass, part of the Caliber family of automotive repair and service brands, has announced the acquisition of Arrow Auto Glass, an auto glass service provider headquartered in Kingston, Pa. The acquisition expands Caliber Auto Glass’s reach into four additional states, bringing its presence to 44 of the lower 48 states.

The acquisition builds on Caliber Auto Glass’s network of auto glass repair, replacement and calibration services. Through its trained technicians and mobile service capabilities, the company provides windshield chip repairs, windshield and other vehicle glass replacements, and advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) calibration services.

Caliber Auto Glass supports commercial fleet customers and works with major insurance providers to help simplify the repair process. As modern vehicles increasingly rely on cameras and sensors integrated into windshields, proper glass replacement and calibration play an important role in vehicle safety.

Caliber Auto Glass’s services are designed to address evolving repair requirements while offering customers convenient access to quality care, backed by a limited lifetime nationwide warranty on eligible glass repairs and replacements.

“Arrow has built a strong regional business with a dedicated team and a longstanding commitment to its customers,” said Troy Mason, senior vice president and general manager of Caliber Auto Glass. “We are excited to welcome Arrow’s teammates to the Caliber family. This acquisition allows us to extend our reach into new markets while continuing to focus on the quality, safety and service our customers depend on.”

Arrow Auto Glass has served customers throughout the eastern United States for many years, establishing a reputation for auto glass repair, replacement and recalibration services. The companies will continue operating separately in the near term, with plans for Arrow to integrate into Caliber Auto Glass in the future.

“We are incredibly proud of our Arrow team,” said Bill Cogswell, president of Arrow Auto Glass. “Their commitment to supporting one another and, most importantly, our customers is what drives us each and every day. Joining with Caliber will provide additional resources, opportunities for our teammates and a continued commitment to servicing our customers.”

The acquisition reflects Caliber Auto Glass’s focus on expanding its service network while investing in the expertise, technology and resources needed to support drivers as vehicle repair requirements evolve.

articles.title: AASP/NJ Offers Two-Night “DC Circuits Analysis” Training Event
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: Modern vehicles are rolling computers, and mastering automotive electrical diagnostics is a necessity. To give New Jersey technicians a competitive edge, the Alliance of Automotive Service Providers of New Jersey (AASP/NJ) is sponsoring an intensive, two-night, hands-on training event focused on DC circuits analysis in December.

Presented by Petty Diagnostics and Technical Services’ Tom Petty Sr. and Tommy Petty Jr. (also of Petty Motorworks, AASP/NJ’s 2026 Mechanical Shop of the Year), “DC Circuits Analysis: From Ohm’s Law to Circuit Diagnosis” will be held Dec. 2-3 from 6 to 10 p.m. at Bella’s Pizza in Waretown, N.J.

Designed for rising techs looking to strengthen their skills and seasoned pros aiming to sharpen diagnostic speed, this course bridges classroom theory and real-world bay experience. From the fundamentals of Ohm’s Law to pinpointing circuit faults, attendees will be ready to tackle electrical problems.
By the end of the two-night course, technicians will learn how to:
- Demystify DC fundamentals: Grasp how voltage, current and resistance interact in automotive circuits.
- Put Ohm’s Law to work: Apply core electrical formulas to everyday diagnostic challenges.
- Decode complex circuits: Identify series and parallel circuits and calculate total resistance.
- Predict current behavior: Understand how shifts in voltage and resistance impact current flow.
- Navigate schematics: Read automotive electrical diagrams and trace current paths.
- Maximize meter mastery: Set up and use a digital volt-ohm meter (DVOM) for accurate readings.
- Pinpoint faults fast: Perform voltage, voltage drop and resistance tests.
- Diagnose with confidence: Interpret test data to isolate opens, shorts and excessive resistance.
AASP/NJ members pay $125 each; nonmember shops pay $150 per person. Shop owners will be admitted FREE with the purchase of at least one registration.
Space is limited and preregistration is required. Register at aaspnj.org/events.
To learn more about AASP/NJ and member benefits, visit aaspnj.org.

articles.title: Boyd to investors on Q3 total losses, TCOR, and repairable claims volumes
articles.author: Lurah Lowery

paras.en: Boyd Group President and CEO Brian Kaner said Wednesday that there is positive momentum in the industry to push total losses down.

Kaner made the comment during the company’s Q3 earnings call with investors. When asked how raising total loss thresholds impacts total loss rates, Kaner said he thinks rates could decrease with more regulation.
“If you see people raising thresholds to 85%, those borderline total losses will end up becoming repairable vehicles again and ultimately help our business,” he said.

“Total losses are getting a tremendous amount of attention in the industry right now. We know that it’s not a great customer experience. There’s more people that are upside down in loans right now, so if their car gets totaled, they end up not only not being able to get a car, but they end up writing a check to get out of the car that they’re actually in. We know that it’s not a great experience. I think many people are picking up on that, inclusive of the insurance carriers.”
He added that attrition after total losses is higher than after repairable claims, which has gotten the attention of insurance carriers and OEMs.

“If you trust the data that’s out there, the data that CCC would reflect or that JD Power reflects, is 40% of people after a total loss event switch insurance carriers, so the attrition after a total loss event versus a repair event that’s 7% is super high,” Kaner said.
He said Q3 claims data continues to point to a more stable operating environment, with repairable claims volumes estimated to be down 1–3% year over year.
Kaner also shared that Boyd saw a sequential improvement in total cost of repair (TCOR) in Q3.

“We said for quite some time that the underlying metrics behind TCOR were still moving as they normally move,” he said. “We still saw normal pricing increases on the labor side. We still saw normal price movement on parts through the inflationary environment that we’re in. And what had been muting that was just the year-over-year impact of more total losses, so bigger tickets coming out of the repair set driving down or mixing down the overall TCOR. We saw that level out in Q3, and we continue to see it now stable as we get into the fourth quarter. That’s allowing the underlying movement and price to actually illuminate.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Part of what’s driving TCOR up, Kaner said, is an increase in calibration services.

“We continue to see a higher penetration rate of calibration services on the average ticket that we’re seeing, and all of those things are starting to move the ticket back in a more positive direction,” he said. “I would say still muted from the, call it 4%, that we expect, but certainly moving its way back towards then.”

A press release on Q3 earnings results adds that “volume gains driven by the strength of the company’s performance and insurer relationships contributed to positive same-store sales growth during the quarter of 2.2%, complemented by a modest increase in total cost of repair.”
Kaner told investors that self-pay jobs are growing at a greater pace than insurance volume, though it’s growing off a much smaller base. He said the average self-pay ticket is much lower.
“Our focus today still remains on providing great service for the insurance partners that we do business with,” he said.
Regarding general Q3 earnings, Boyd reported a 28% revenue increase supported by the addition of Joe Hudson’s.
Kaner said the focus with integrating Joe Hudson’s is now on improving client scores to drive incremental volume and ensuring stores have adequate staffing.
Kaner also told investors that Boyd has 34 new startup locations planned for the next 12 months.

articles.title: NHTSA’s White to collision repairers: ‘You are the final checkpoint’
articles.author: Teresa Moss

paras.en: The collision repair industry has a bigger role in the national vehicle conversation than the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has historically recognized, Lee White, NHTSA’s deputy administrator, said during the Society of Collision Repair Specialists’ (SCRS) OEM Summit held during the 2026 SEMA Show.

“I’m excited to be here speaking with skilled craftsmen and women who bring vehicles back to life after they’ve had an accident,” White said. “When done right, your work is often underappreciated, even though it is the product of hard-won expertise.”
NHTSA exists because there is risk every time someone drives on U.S. roadways, White said.
In the 1970s, about 70,000 Americans died a year on U.S. roadways, he said. That number was reduced to about 39,000 in 2024, and the estimate is below 37,000 in 2025.

“That is a lot of progress, particularly when you consider how many more cars and trucks are on the road, as well as the miles that we drive,” he said. “NHTSA cannot take all the credit for this improvement. Many players have contributed, from local governments to the major vehicle manufacturers. There is a lot of work still to be done.”
NHTSA Administrator Jonathon Morrison frequently tells his staff that the agency cannot operate in a vacuum, White said.

“We are opening up our doors to all our stakeholders and the experts like those in the room,” White said. “We want to team with you, and we want to work with your team, and we want to hear from you. The collaborative spirit is exactly why I am here today. By working together, we can save lives.”
The Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (FMVSS) conversation typically revolves around how a vehicle is designed, White said.

“But reality tells us a different story,” White said. “A vehicle may be on the road for 15 to 20 years, experiencing multiple collisions and undergoing numerous repairs over its useful life. From NHTSA’s perspective, we must think deeply about how to preserve the safety performance engineered into a vehicle throughout its entire lifespan, and certify that there’s no degradation.”
NHTSA research on automatic emergency braking, for example, shows the technology prevents crashes, he said.

“We accept that these systems create a measurable safety benefit,” White said. “Preserving that capability after a collision must become a core part of how we think about vehicle safety. If a system was producing a measurable reduction in crash risk before a crash, our expectation must be that it will continue to do so after the vehicle leaves your repair facility.”

White added that looking for a warning light on the dashboard is not enough to safely evaluate vehicle damage. He said shops must verify that safety systems are performing before returning the vehicle to customers.
The complexity will grow as the vehicle fleet transitions to autonomous vehicles, he said.
White pointed to a recent partnership between NHTSA and SAE to expedite the development of data-driven AV performance standards.

“As we move toward vehicles assuming more of the driving task, the integrity of a collision repair becomes even more consequential,” White said. “The collision repair industry must start preparing for this right now. If we are ultimately going to trust a vehicle to make safety-critical decisions, it is absolutely essential to know that its sensing and decision-making capabilities have been properly restored following a collision.”
NHTSA needs data to better navigate the future, he said. He added this provides an opportunity for the collision repair industry and NHTSA to collaborate.

“Your facilities see damaged vehicles every day,” White said. “You are sitting on a potentially valuable source of safety information that historically hasn’t been part of the research ecosystem. The information coming out of a repair process could help NHTSA and manufacturers significantly better understand how safety systems perform in the real world.”
NHTSA wants comments from the collision industry, White said.

This includes during a 90-day comment period that will follow an ADAS Workshop on Aftermarket Modifications and ADAS Performance event Dec. 10. The event will bring together OEMs, Tier 1 suppliers, engineering firms, academics, and SEMA to talk about the issues, White said.

“We believe that this event will be an important step toward solutions,” White said. “Reconciling the different interests of all those involved may be challenging, but all involved can certainly agree that keeping safety is paramount.”
Aaron Schulenburg, SCRS executive director, sat down with White during the OEM Summit. He noted that NHTSA organically found individuals on SCRS’ ADAS Governing Council to join the event.
White said NHTSA will read every comment submitted following the event.
“Submit your comments,” White added. “We want to hear from you.”
Schulenburg asked what repair information might help NHTSA in the future.

“How can we learn more about certain repair issues that this room is having in terms of what needs to get back to the OEMs and what we can do to improve the safety profile,” White said. “It’s a matter of turning data into real-world steps we can take to make our roads safer, to make the vehicles perform at a safer rate, and to make our drivers’ behavior better. That’s our goal.”
The collision industry faces pressure that can lead to repairs that don’t necessarily restore the systems, Schulenburg responded.

“I think that’s where the data question comes in: how do we use that to connect the dots to incentivize proper repairs to restore the safety rather than allowing that pressure, the cost mitigation to influence the industry to move in different directions?, he asked.
White said he hopes that conversation becomes a part of the Dec. 10 event.

“The people in this room, you care about doing repairs the right way,” White said. “We want our rules and regulations to encourage that. We can’t make choices because of financial pressure. Financial pressure, wherever it’s coming from — internal to your company or from industry, if it’s coming from insurance, wherever that pressure point’s coming, it can’t be at the expense of safety. We can never let a vehicle go out of our shops and be at risk safety-wise because we chose cost.”
The event should identify what research is missing and what steps should be taken in the next 12 months, he said.
“We’ve got to make sure that we’ve got the voice, we’ve got the comments, we’ve got the gaps identified, so that we know what we’ve got to do,” he said.
A question from the audience asked White how NHTSA tracks alternative parts.

“If you see something, say something,” White said. “Go to the NHTSA website. You can fill out a form and let us know that you have an issue with a part that you’re concerned about. Whether it’s a comment that we issue from a conference or a notice of proposed rulemaking, there’s people in NHTSA that look at that and take that seriously.”

NHTSA has been raising the performance bar in other ways recently, White said. This includes incorporating new ADAS evaluations, such as automatic emergency braking, into its New Car Assessment Program (NCAP).
Automakers and vehicle safety groups told Congress last year that NCAP had fallen behind other countries and wasn’t rating new safety technologies fast enough.

White said under Morrison, NHTSA is evaluating not only whether it has the equipment but if it also performs. He pointed to an AEB final rule that specifies vehicle and pedestrian avoidance performance benchmarks on vehicles by 2029.

“Administrator Morrison has made it clear that many of our past regulations were designed when no one envisioned modern safety technologies, meaning that the technology of the future is often tethered to the regulations of the past,” White said. “To address this, under the leadership of President Trump and Transportation Secretary Duffy, NHTSA is diligently working to update the FMVSS to account for these new designs, prioritizing safety requirements and the performance of those requirements over design specifications.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The repair industry must also evolve as performance expectations become more sophisticated, White said.

“The critical question must shift from ‘did we calibrate it?’ to ‘have we restored its performance?’ Manufacturers, regulators, and repairers all have a shared role in establishing confidence that these systems continue to deliver their intended safety benefit after a crash,” White said.
Schulenburg asked whether NHTSA had any guidance on how the collision industry can navigate pressure it faces in the claims environment. For example, pressure to use alternative parts.
“Our worry as an industry is that oftentimes that may produce an outcome that doesn’t preserve the safety that you’ve worked so hard to create in the standards,” Schulenburg said.
White responded, “You are under tremendous pressure to cut costs. That can’t come at the expense of safety. Safety always has to be foundational.”
Affordability is also part of that equation, he added. Technology advancement must consider the cost of repair, he said.
Recently, an OEM announced six new model types that will sell below $40,000, he said.

“The message of affordability is a loud one,” White said. “How do we do that? What we don’t want is a safety system that only performs like it’s on the showroom floor. We can’t do that at the repair shops. That’s not an acceptable business model. How do we strike that balance? There are still a lot of details to work out, but we don’t want to put in any safety risk in that process.”

Schulenburg responded, “I think when consumers have to assume parts of the cost of the repair that they otherwise expected to be covered by a claim, those are pieces of affordability that don’t always get addressed. You’re obviously engaging with the repair community and the manufacturer community. Do you also engage with the insurance community around these topics?”
White said NHTSA has ongoing communications with the insurance industry as well. It also tries to stay up to date on trends.
Deadly counterfeit airbags are an example of how a decision made during a repair can determine whether a safety system protects someone or actually injures them, White said.

“That’s the lesson that NHTSA has learned and what collision repairers need to hear is that the traceability, the authenticity, and the suitability of the safety-critical replacement components are paramount,” he said. “We understand the pressure from the insurance companies on repairs to seek out alternative parts, lower their costs. But there’s an equal reason of concern when dealing with alternative safety sensors, cameras, and radar units.”

NHTSA identified an 11th death caused by a counterfeit airbag part from China in September. The agency urges owners of used vehicles that have previously been in a crash with an airbag deployment since 2020 to have their vehicle inspected.
The agency banned the importation and sale of these DTN60DB inflators earlier this year; the first ban NHTSA issued in more than two decades.
White said the sellers of counterfeit parts have short-term business models.
“They pop up, they disappear,” he said. “They go out of business, and then six months later they surface. We shut that one down, and then two days later they open up another marketplace.”
These are trends buyers can look for when looking for a reputable parts seller, he said.
Schulenburg responded that authorized supply channels play an important role in protecting against counterfeit parts.
He asked whether there is a risk for other counterfeit parts such as cameras, sensors, and radars.

“That’s a global threat as far as knockoffs and noncompliant equipment,” White responded. “We’re going to have to constantly be sure that we’ve got the right standards, sure that their performance levels are validated.”
Every OEM has different technology developments, he said. He added that each has a different level of performance.

“A lidar advancement means maybe it’s six months ahead of the radar and it’s a little bit ahead of the camera,” White said. “How do we make sure that that system performs like it was designed, at that same year model with similar equipment and similar mileage?”
There have to be some procedures and processes in place to keep technology performing after a collision, he said.
He noted that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has published some guidelines.
“NHTSA hasn’t done that in terms of the technology,” White said. “We are going to go after the performance of the system.”
Federal law prohibits any motor vehicle repair business from knowingly making a device or design element of a vehicle inoperative, he said.

“While the concept of not rendering inoperative a federally required safety system is not new, a lot of the technology found in modern vehicles is,” White said. “When a vehicle safety system performance depends on cameras, radar, software, precise mounting tolerances, calibration, and interconnected systems, the responsibility of the repairer is more complex than ever before.”
“Rendering inoperative” is a term used by NHTSA that defines the degradation of a safety system to where it doesn’t perform as it should.

Schulenburg pointed out that the rendering inoperative discussion historically has been focused on safety systems such as airbags and seatbelts. He asked how this could change with the advancement of technical safety systems.
“What’s happening is we’re moving toward a situation where the vehicle is going to be able to operate itself,” White said.
He added that the discussion of rendering inoperable grows in the scenario.
Schulenburg asked whether the recent elections will change the way that NHTSA operates.

“I’ll go back to the 100 people that are going to be killed in crashes today,” White said. “They’re not worried about elections. They want the safety equipment to work. The NHTSA mission transcends the politics in Washington, D.C. I’ve never met a team of more committed people working every day on safety.”
Looking forward, White said training technicians for future technology is one of the most important pieces for the collision repair industry.
“That’s where the energy needs to be, so that we’re prepared, so that as the technology comes out in 2027, 2028, 2029, and these model years start rolling out, we’re ready,” White said.
Collision repairers touch vehicles at a unique, critical moment after something goes wrong and before vehicles go back on the road, White said.

“There are profound opportunities for the collision repair community to become a more meaningful partner in NHTSA’s safety mission,” he added. “If there’s one thing I want everyone in the collision repair business in this room to understand about your role in vehicle safety, it is this: you are the final checkpoint. The safety standards we write and the system automakers engineer rely entirely on your expertise to ensure endurance throughout that vehicle’s life.”

Aaron Schulenburg, SCRS executive director, and Lee White, NHTSA’s deputy administrator, discuss the collision repair industry during SCRS’ OEM Summit at the 2026 SEMA Show (Lurah Lowery/Repairer Driven News).

articles.title: Free Webinar: Preventing and Curing Brake Pulsations
articles.author: Doug Kaufman

paras.en: Experienced technicins have seen it dozens of times. A customer comes back after a recent brake service, complaining about pulsation or judder when braking. The problem is often blamed on “warped rotors,” but the underlying cause may involve component quality, measurement errors, or improper installation practices.

In a free webinar to be held Thursday, November 19, 2026 from 2-3 pm Eastern, Brake & Front End’s Andrew Markel and Aumovio’s Doug Rennie will examine recommended service procedures for European, Asian, and domestic vehicles, with practical guidance on diagnosis, preparation and installation to help technicians diagnose problems accurately, perform more effective repairs and prevent future comebacks.
- Rotor and brake pad quality: Understanding how component selection and condition affect braking performance.
- Lateral runout diagnosis: Identifying excessive runout and its potential causes.
- Rotor measurements: Properly measuring rotor thickness and thickness variation to identify potential problems.
- Hub preparation: Ensuring clean, properly prepared mounting surfaces for accurate rotor installation.
- Installation best practices: Applying proper wheel-fastener torque and using brake lubricants correctly to help prevent future brake pulsation and judder complaints.

articles.title: The Group Launches Toys for Tots Drive
articles.author: Doug Kaufman

paras.en: For the 15th consecutive year, participating Automotive Parts Services Group (The Group) members are supporting the U.S. Marine Corps Reserve Toys for Tots campaign by collecting toy and monetary donations for children in need in their communities.

“Over the years, our Toys for Tots partnership has continued to grow as we collect toys and raise funds to bring holiday cheer to children in need across the country,” said John Marcum, director of marketing at Federated Auto Parts. “The Group’s members have played an important role in growing the campaign through their commitment to promoting the program and encouraging community support. What began as a holiday effort has grown into a year-round initiative. We extend our sincere thanks to the Federated Alliance, The Pronto Network and our supplier partners for their ongoing generosity and commitment to this cause.”

paras.en: The Group Raises Over $4 Million for Toys For Tots

Since partnering with the U.S. Marine Corps Reserve Toys for Tots Program, The Group, its members and vendor partners have helped raise over $4 million for Toys for Tots. In addition to toy donations at participating locations, financial contributions can be made online by visiting The Group’s Toys for Tots website and clicking on “Make a Donation.” Donors can use a credit card securely or print out a form and mail it with a check made payable to Toys for Tots.

“All donations made online or at participating member locations are distributed in the area where the toys and money are collected, helping make the holidays brighter for deserving children in their own communities,” said Marcum.

Last year, the campaign delivered 24 million toys to nearly 11 million children and since 1947, the Marine Toys for Tots Foundation has distributed more than 732 million toys to more than 325 million children.

articles.title: The Downside of Regenerative Braking
articles.author: Joe Keene

paras.en: Regenerative braking allows electric vehicles to recover energy during deceleration. Instead of converting all vehicle momentum into heat at the brake rotors, the electric motor acts as a generator. This slows the vehicle while returning some energy to the battery.
The process can significantly reduce the use of conventional friction brakes. However, reduced brake usage can also create maintenance challenges involving corrosion and component operation.
On conventional internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, brake pads regularly contact the rotors during braking. This friction helps remove light surface corrosion from the rotor faces.
EVs with aggressive regenerative braking may use their friction brakes less frequently. Exposure to moisture, road salt and humidity can then allow corrosion to develop on the rotor surfaces.
EV Regenerative Braking and Rotor Corrosion
Light surface rust is not necessarily a problem because normal brake applications can remove it. However, corrosion can progress when friction brakes are not used regularly.
Over time, heavier rust, pitting and scaling can develop on the rotors. Once the rotor surfaces deteriorate significantly, normal brake applications may not restore their condition.
Reduced friction brake usage can also extend brake pad life. However, brake components can develop problems unrelated to friction material wear.

Corrosion may form around brake pad hardware, caliper brackets, slide pins and other components. Pads can become restricted in their brackets, while caliper components may develop problems from limited movement.
As a result, brake components may require replacement because of corrosion or restricted movement rather than normal wear.
How Regenerative and Friction Braking Work Together
Electric vehicles still require conventional hydraulic friction brakes to maintain stopping performance.

Regenerative braking may become reduced or unavailable under certain operating conditions. These include a fully charged battery, very cold battery temperatures, vehicle stability control intervention or certain system faults.
EV braking systems blend regenerative braking with conventional hydraulic friction braking to provide the stopping performance drivers expect.
This makes conventional brake system condition an important consideration, even when regenerative braking reduces normal friction brake usage.
EV Brake Inspection and Maintenance Considerations
Technicians should account for reduced friction brake usage when inspecting electric vehicle braking systems.
Measuring brake pad thickness alone may not provide a complete picture of component condition.

EV regenerative braking improves efficiency by recovering energy and can substantially extend brake pad life. However, reduced friction brake usage can also increase the potential for corrosion and restricted component movement.
Brake condition assessments should account for both friction material wear and the effects of limited brake usage.

articles.title: Are We Asking the Wrong Questions About AI?
articles.author: Brandi Gangel

paras.en: Want to Know What AI Means for Your Business?

Join Babcox Media and SmarterX on Wednesday, December 9, at 2 pm ET for a free webinar, The State of AI for Business: 5 Things Every Leader Needs to Know, featuring AI expert Paul Roetzer. Discover the developments that matter, where the opportunities are, and how to put AI to work in your business. Register for the webinar

I’ve been in marketing long enough to remember when having a website was considered innovative. Then came social media, mobile marketing, programmatic advertising, and the endless parade of technologies promising to change everything. Some did. Some didn’t. And some just gave us more dashboards to stare at. But artificial intelligence? This one feels different.

At MAICON, journalist and author Kevin Roose delivered a thought-provoking keynote titled How to Feel the AGI, drawing on his reporting and his book, The AGI Chronicles. I haven’t read the book yet, but his presentation gave me plenty to think about.
Specifically, are we asking the right questions about AI? Or are we still thinking too small?
We’re Using AI. But Are We Really Getting It?

Roose introduced the concept of “feeling the AGI”—understanding the magnitude and speed of artificial intelligence’s evolution and adjusting how we think, work, and plan accordingly. AGI stands for Artificial General Intelligence. In simple terms, it’s the idea of AI is capable of performing a broad range of intellectual tasks at or beyond human ability.
According to Roose, the people closest to developing these technologies aren’t simply anticipating change. They’re already organizing their lives and businesses around it. That got my attention.

In the automotive aftermarket, we’re pretty good at adapting. Supply chain disruptions? We’ve managed them. Changing consumer behavior? We’re tracking it. E-commerce, evolving vehicle technology, shifting distribution models? We’ve been navigating those curves for years. But AI isn’t just another curve in the road. It has the potential to change the vehicle, the driver, and the destination. And no, I don’t mean autonomous cars.

One of Roose’s observations really stuck with me: Most people are still using incredibly sophisticated AI as a glorified search engine. We’ve all used it to polish an email, summarize a meeting, or generate a few ideas. Helpful? Absolutely. Transformational? Not exactly. The real opportunity isn’t simply getting AI to do what we’re already doing, only faster. It’s reimagining what’s possible. Consider what that could mean for the aftermarket.

What if we could identify emerging customer needs before they become obvious in sales reports? What if we could connect purchasing behavior, vehicle data, market conditions, and audience insights to create more meaningful customer experiences? What if sales and marketing teams spent less time gathering information and more time acting on it?

These aren’t promises that AI can magically solve every business challenge tomorrow. But I’m proud to say they’re the kinds of questions my colleagues at Babcox Media are asking today. Because we know the competitive advantage won’t come from simply having access to AI. It will come from knowing what to do with it.

We’ve always known that understanding your audience is the foundation of effective marketing. That’s the entire foundation of B2B media! What’s changing is our ability to turn information into intelligence, and intelligence into action. AI creates opportunities to connect data across systems, departments, and platforms in ways that were previously too complex, too expensive, or too time-consuming. For an industry as information-rich and relationship-driven as the automotive aftermarket, that’s exciting.

paras.en: But there’s a catch. AI doesn’t automatically make bad data good. And it certainly doesn’t replace sound business judgment. The real value comes from combining quality data, industry expertise, creativity, and technology to make smarter decisions and deliver more relevant experiences.

For all the excitement surrounding AI, Roose also addressed its risks, including the challenges of controlling increasingly autonomous systems. His message wasn’t simply to embrace the technology. It was to recognize that we have a responsibility to shape how it’s used, and I couldn’t agree more. Technology is an enabler. It can help us understand audiences, identify opportunities, improve efficiency, and deliver better results. But it doesn’t replace relationships, trust, creativity, quality, or accountability. In the aftermarket, where relationships and reputation matter enormously, those qualities aren’t optional. They’re our advantage.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The goal shouldn’t be to remove people from the equation. It should be to give talented people better information, stronger capabilities, and more time to focus on the work that actually moves businesses forward.
Roose wrapped up his keynote with a reminder that resonated with me: We aren’t passive observers of technological change. We have a role in shaping what comes next. That’s an important distinction.

The automotive aftermarket has never been short on ingenuity, resilience, or entrepreneurial spirit. We know how to solve problems. We know how to adapt. And we know that standing still is rarely a winning strategy. AI presents another opportunity to put those strengths to work.

At Babcox Media, we’re approaching this evolution with curiosity, intention, and a healthy respect for human insight. We’re challenging ourselves to think differently about how data, technology, and creativity can work together to create meaningful business outcomes. And we’re learning along the way. Because maybe the most important question isn’t, “What can AI do for us?” Maybe it’s, “What could we accomplish if we stopped limiting our thinking to what we’ve always done?”
And if you’re thinking about what this means for your business, your customers, or our industry, I’d love to compare notes.

What began as a holiday effort has grown into a year-round initiative. We extend our sincere thanks to the Federated Alliance, The Pronto Network and our supplier partners for their ongoing generosity and commitment to this cause.”

paras.en: Dorman Products Inc. continues expanding its aftermarket product offerings with repair solutions that address common failure points in original equipment parts. The company recently launched a new OE FIX engine oil filter housing (part number 926-611) for select Genesis, Hyundai and Kia vehicles.

“Dorman continues to launch new innovations that expand the breadth of our product offerings and provide customers with improved solutions to common original equipment problems,” said Eric Luftig, Dorman’s President, Light Duty. “Our OE FIX products are designed to give technicians greater confidence that a repair will be completed right the first time, with a more durable solution that helps reduce the risk of repeat failures and costly comebacks. By continuing to identify common failure points and develop better repair solutions, we create new opportunities for our customers while helping them deliver greater value to the technicians and vehicle owners they serve.”

paras.en: Dorman Addresses Common Oil Filter Housing Failures

The original equipment oil filter housing on certain Genesis, Hyundai and Kia vehicles uses plastic that can warp. Prolonged exposure to heat and chemicals under the hood can cause the plastic to degrade. Over time, the housing can leak oil or crack.
Replacing the failed part with another original equipment housing can leave the vehicle vulnerable to the same failure.

Dorman manufactures the 926-611 OE FIX replacement from high-pressure die-cast aluminum for a more durable repair. The housing includes the required mounting gaskets, premium seals, an oil filter element and an oil filter cap. These components provide technicians with everything needed for a complete installation.
Dorman engineered the product in the United States to precise specifications that help resist future leaks and provide reliable service.
Company Expands Oil Filter Housing Portfolio
The 926-611 builds on the performance of Dorman’s patented 926-959 aluminum oil filter housing. That product serves a wide range of Chrysler, Dodge, Jeep, Ram and Volkswagen vehicles.
Launched in 2023, the 926-959 has become one of the company’s most successful offerings.

Dorman has expanded its portfolio of oil filter housings, adapters, coolers, assemblies and seals. The product line addresses common original equipment failure points and aims to help technicians avoid repeat repairs.
The new engine oil filter housing is among the Dorman OE FIX solutions featured in the company’s sixth OE FIX Guide. It joins the thousands of OE FIX solutions Dorman currently offers.
The guide highlights products with improved designs, time-saving features and cost-efficient repair options.

articles.title: NAPA Opens First Highly Automated Reverse Logistics Center
articles.author: Mary DellaValle

paras.en: NAPA recently celebrated the grand opening of its York Reverse Logistics Center (RLC), marking the debut of the first highly automated facility of its kind within the NAPA network and an important milestone in the company’s ongoing supply chain transformation.

The 400,000-square-foot center combines more than 100 robots and advanced automation technology with a skilled local workforce to process returns, cores and inventory for redistribution across the NAPA Northeast distribution network.

The center began operations earlier this year and is designed to accelerate returns processing, helping get parts back into inventory faster and improving availability for NAPA stores, repair professionals and their customers, the company said. The new facility, which can support 250,000 unique SKUs, is expected to reduce the time needed to prepare inventory for redistribution by 43% and support inventory accuracy up to 99.5%.

Leaders from NAPA and corporate parent Genuine Parts Company (GPC) were joined by York Mayor Sandie Walker, state and local elected officials, the York County Economic Alliance, community partners and teammates for a ribbon-cutting ceremony and tours of the facility at 500 Willow Springs Lane.

“York is the first step in a broader modernization of the NAPA supply chain,” said Justin Ducharme, executive vice president, supply chain, NAPA. “By combining innovative technology with the expertise of our teammates, we’re creating a more efficient operation that helps keep parts moving to the customers and repair professionals who rely on us every day.”

During the ceremony, the GPC Foundation presented a $2,500 Good Neighbor grant to United Way of York County. The grant supports the foundation’s mobility priority and reflects a shared belief that reliable transportation opens access to jobs, health care and stronger family life.

As the first highly automated reverse logistics center within the NAPA network, RLC represents an important milestone in the company’s efforts to enhance operational capabilities and support the growing needs of customers across the Northeast, the company said.

articles.title: Advance Auto Parts Opens First Store in King of Prussia

The company marked the opening of the store at 125 W. Dekalb Pike with a ribbon-cutting ceremony alongside local officials and representatives from Central Montco Technical High School who were on site to accept a donation for the school’s automotive technology program.

The donation will help students gain hands-on experience, training and career opportunities through the school’s automotive technology programs. Skilled automotive technicians continue to be in high demand, with approximately 70,000 openings projected annually through 2034, according to U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

“We’re excited to bring Advance Auto Parts to King of Prussia and open our first store in the community,” said Eli Rosa, regional vice president, Advance Auto Parts. “In addition to serving local customers, this market hub will help strengthen support for professional technicians and nearby shops across the area. We’re proud to mark the occasion by supporting Central Montco Technical High School and the programs that help students prepare for automotive technician careers.”

“We appreciate Advance Auto Parts’ support of career and technical education,” said Craig Robinson, administrative director at Central Montco Technical High School. “This donation helps support the hands-on learning experiences that are at the core of our automotive technology program and gives students opportunities to build skills they’ll use long after graduation.”

The new store also serves as a market hub – a centralized facility designed to improve parts availability and same-day fulfillment across a network of stores, enhancing hard parts coverage for professional customers, Advance Auto Parts said.

articles.title: How did Cleopatra really die?
articles.author: Olivia Maule

paras.en: The death of Cleopatra is among the most famous in history. In 31 B.C., the Egyptian queen and her Roman ally and lover, Mark Antony, lost the Battle of Actium to Octavian, who would later become Rome's first emperor, Augustus. The following summer, Cleopatra was captured during a Roman ambush inside her royal tomb in Alexandria.

According to Octavian’s account, rather than facing the disgrace of defeat, the queen allowed a venomous asp snake to bite her and quickly succumbed to its poison. Some Roman writers, such as the historian Velleius Paterculus, repeated that story without question.

But others were far less certain of this account, calling it Roman propaganda to cement Octavian's rise to power. And most historians today doubt that a snake was involved at all. So how did Cleopatra die?
Live Science spoke with experts, who told us that the queen's death is still shrouded in mystery.

"We cannot know for sure exactly how Cleopatra died," Prudence Jones, a professor of classics at Montclair State University in New Jersey and author of "Cleopatra: A Sourcebook" (University of Oklahoma Press, 2006), told Live Science in an email.
What historians largely agree on is that Cleopatra VII, the last queen of Egypt's Ptolemaic dynasty, took her own life and that she chose a method that left her body composed and dignified.

Physical evidence of Cleopatra's death is elusive. Much of Alexandria's royal quarter now lies underwater, and underwater archaeologist Franck Goddio, who has been excavating it, hasn't found the queen's mausoleum, Jones said. Even if Cleopatra's remains surfaced, bones would be unlikely to show evidence of snake venom, she added, noting that forensics is outside her area of expertise.
Feed your curiosity with an exclusive mystery every week, solved with science and delivered direct to your inbox before it's seen anywhere else.
The best witness may have been Olympus, Cleopatra's personal physician. "Unfortunately, nothing survives of Olympus' account," Jones said.

What does remain is a story told largely by Cleopatra's enemies. The earliest surviving account is a poem by the Roman poet Horace, whose patron was a close friend of Octavian, said Jane Draycott, a historian at the University of Glasgow. His Ode 1.37, written around the time of her death, celebrates Octavian's victory and already pictures the queen handling serpents — yet it ends with grudging admiration for a woman who refused to be paraded as a trophy.

Following her capture, Cleopatra was held under military guard. By then, she had already tried to end her life twice. Cleopatra had tried to stab herself when Roman soldiers broke into the mausoleum where she had barricaded herself, and she later tried to starve herself, stopping only after Octavian threatened her children.

To Draycott, those attempts leave little doubt that Cleopatra would rather die than live as a captive. "She does not want to be a prisoner; she does not want to be led through the streets of Rome in triumph as a defeated foe," she told Live Science.

In the Greco-Roman world, suicide didn't carry the stigma it later acquired under Christianity, she added. "It was a way of wiping the slate clean, removing any shame, any disgrace from yourself." After the defeat of his remaining forces at Alexandria and hearing a false report of Cleopatra's death, Antony was the first of the two lovers to die by suicide.

According to the Greek biographer Plutarch, who based his account on that of Cleopatra's personal physician, Cleopatra visited Antony's tomb, bathed, ate and sent Octavian a sealed letter asking to be buried beside Antony, signaling that she meant to die. Octavian realized what was happening and sent messengers rushing to her, but they arrived too late. They found her dead in her royal regalia, with her attendants Iras and Charmion dying beside her.

Jones has compiled what ancient historians, biographers, geographers and physicians wrote about Cleopatra's death. Every source mentions a snakebite, but several also suggest other possibilities, including a poisonous ointment, poison hidden in a hollow hairpin, and snake venom poured into a wound the queen made by biting herself. Only one of these writers, the geographer Strabo, was alive when Cleopatra died, and the only people in the room with her died, too.

The Roman historian Cassius Dio wrote that the sole clue was a pair of faint pricks on her arm. That doesn't settle much, however. "A cobra bite can appear as two small puncture wounds, but not all cobra bites appear this way and not all double puncture wounds result from snakebites," Jones said.

Jones traces the snake version of the story to Octavian, who was in Alexandria when Cleopatra died. Plutarch reported that an image of Cleopatra with an asp clinging to her was carried in Octavian's triumphal procession in Rome. "Octavian, however, was Cleopatra's enemy and for that reason we may not want to accept his account uncritically," Jones said.

Draycott suggested another possible source of confusion: Snake-shaped jewelry was fashionable in Alexandria at the time, so Romans viewing an effigy of the queen may have mistaken a snake bracelet for a real snake.

Draycott doesn't think one snake could have killed all three women. Jones is less certain. Snakes don't inject the same amount of venom with every bite, and some "dry bites" deliver none at all, Jones said. "On the other hand, I don't think it is impossible, as the body of a cobra contains enough venom to kill multiple people," she added.

The general view among historians, Draycott said, is that Cleopatra took some kind of poison — one that worked quickly and didn't cause seizures or vomiting. The absence of these symptoms is telling: An asp is believed to be what is now known as the Egyptian cobra (Naja haje), whose venom causes a slow, agonizing death with respiratory failure.

Cleopatra likely would have had other means, then. Alexandria was the Mediterranean's center of scientific study, and texts from the period, such as Nicander's "Theriaca," catalog venomous animals, Jones noted. Cleopatra's father, Ptolemy XII, even consulted the pharmacologist Zopyrus about antidotes. Plutarch claimed that Cleopatra personally oversaw experiments that observed the effects of deadly poisons on condemned prisoners.

Still, that claim and other poison stories should be read with caution, Draycott said, because they draw on Roman stereotypes about women. In the Roman view, "manly men will battle with swords," while women, seen as "deceitful and weak" at this time, were thought to kill in secret. "They'll sneak it into your food," Draycott said, summing up the stereotype.

Roman writers were equally suspicious. Poisoning allegations dogged the Hellenistic dynasties of ancient Egypt and the neighboring Seleucid kingdom, as well as Rome's own imperial family. Some were probably true, Draycott said, but others may have been foodborne illnesses or other health conditions people didn't understand.
The method may remain a mystery, but for most historians, the motive doesn't change: Cleopatra chose to die on her own terms.

She holds a B.A. in biology and a B.S. in anthropology from the University of Florida and completed a master's degree in science communication at U.C. Santa Cruz. articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 mission forever changed our view of Jupiter
articles.author: Brandon Specktor

paras.en: This Wednesday (Nov. 18), humanity's most distant spacecraft will hit a new milestone. NASA's Voyager 1 probe, which has been exploring our solar system at increasingly remote depths since 1977, will reach 16.09 billion miles (25.89 billion kilometers) from Earth — a distance so vast, it takes light 24 hours to traverse the space between Voyager and our planet.

While we celebrate this achievement on Earth, Voyager 1 will observe its "light-day" in darkness; mission scientists turned off the probe's camera in 1990, immediately after it snapped its iconic "Pale Blue Dot" and "Solar System Family Portrait" images from beyond the orbit of Neptune. But before that, Voyager 1 had already taken tens of thousands of images of our cosmic neighborhood, and some of them totally transformed our understanding of the outer planets.

One of the most significant pieces of Voyager 1's legacy is its trip to Jupiter. From January to April 1979, the probe observed the solar system's largest planet and several of its giant moons up close, reaching a minimum distance of 174,000 miles (280,000 km) in March 1979, according to NASA. As it approached, Voyager snapped a photo of the gas giant every 96 seconds to create this incredible time-lapse movie of Jupiter's turbulent atmosphere.

Voyager observed discrete bands of Jupiter's atmosphere spinning at various speeds and in different directions, like a cosmic Rubik's Cube being twisted by an invisible hand. Clouds speed by as if on conveyor belts as giant, planet-size storms swirl.

Voyager's time-lapse film captures about 60 full days on Jupiter — the equivalent of about a month on Earth, since each Jupiter day is roughly 10 Earth hours —- providing the most comprehensive and high-resolution look at the planet yet. The observations significantly built on the data captured by NASA's Pioneer 10 and 11 Jupiter probes, which launched half a decade prior, showing the planet's atmosphere to be much more dynamic than astronomers realized.

Just before making its closest approach to the planet, Voyager spotted something remarkable: Jupiter had a thin, faint ring system. Made primarily of dust, the rings appeared only when Voyager saw Jupiter backlit by the sun. No telescope had ever seen this before, but ground-based observatories soon confirmed the rings' existence, and Voyager 2 took even clearer pictures of the rings when it reached Jupiter in July 1979.

We now know that all four outer planets — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune — have rings. Today, scientists suspect Jupiter's dusty rings are replenished partially by volcanic eruptions on the planet's volatile moon Io.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

This discovery, too, can be linked to Voyager. While making a close approach to Io, the spacecraft witnessed the first-ever volcanic eruption on a world beyond Earth. This observation showed that moons, not just planets, can be geologically active. In this image, a giant volcano called Loki Patera (the largest volcano on Io, measuring an estimated 125 miles, or 200 km, wide) spews its guts into space.

Taken together, these observations of Jupiter and its moons showed the largest planet and its moons to be a far more dynamic, complicated and chaotic system than anyone had realized. Moreover, the close-up views of these distant worlds made them more than just dots in the sky. It made them fully realized worlds — places to explore, map and eventually visit. Just this week, China's space agency announced its intention to send a lander to Jupiter's moon Callisto in the first-ever landing mission to the Jovian system.

paras.en: Voyager 1's work continues in interstellar space, which it officially reached in 2012. With its camera off, it studies the radiation environment of space using magnetic field and plasma detectors — the last two of its 10 science instruments still receiving power. Scientists suspect the legendary probe will fully run out of power in the 2030s.

Brandon is the space / physics editor at Live Science. With more than 20 years of editorial experience, his writing has appeared in The Washington Post, Reader's Digest, CBS.com, the Richard Dawkins Foundation website and other outlets. He holds a bachelor's degree in creative writing from the University of Arizona, with minors in journalism and media arts. His interests include black holes, asteroids and comets, and the search for extraterrestrial life.

articles.title: 'Out there, moving into the unknown': As Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, scientists reflect on its past — and its future
articles.author: Sharmila Kuthunur

paras.en: NASA's Voyager 1 probe, already the farthest human-made object in space, is about to set another record. On Nov. 18, the spacecraft will be so far from Earth that light, the universe's ultimate speed limit, takes a full 24 hours to reach it.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局的“旅行者1号”探测器已经是太空中距离地球最远的人造物体，它即将再创一项纪录。11月18日，这艘太空船将远离地球，以至于光（宇宙的极限速度）需要整整24小时才能到达它。

paras.en: For researchers who worked on the Voyager program and continue to study its data, the symbolic milestone of being a full light-day from Earth celebrates a mission that continues half a century after it began. Since launching in September 1977, the twin Voyager probes have outlasted many of the engineers who built them, and their flybys of the outer solar system planets remain some of the best close-up observations scientists have of those distant worlds.
paras.zh: 对于曾参与“旅行者”计划并仍在研究其数据的研究人员来说，距离地球一个光日的象征性里程碑是对一项在启动半个世纪后仍在继续的使命的庆祝。自1977年9月发射以来，这对“旅行者”双探测器的寿命已经超过了许多制造它们的工程师，它们对太阳系外行星的飞越仍然是科学家们对这些遥远世界进行的最出色的近距离观测之一。

paras.en: "Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 are transcending generations," Pascal Lee, a planetary scientist at the SETI Institute who was part of the Voyager 2 team at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) during its Neptune flyby in 1989, told Live Science. "Not only is their data relevant, but they themselves are still out there, moving into the unknown."
paras.zh: SETI研究所的行星科学家帕斯卡尔·李（Pascal Lee）在接受《生活科学》采访时表示：“‘旅行者1号’和‘旅行者2号’超越了世代。”1989年‘旅行者2号’飞掠海王星时，他曾是美国宇航局喷气推进实验室（JPL）‘旅行者2号’团队的一员。“它们不仅提供了有价值的数据，而且它们本身仍在太空中，正向未知领域进发。”

paras.en: Here is what the Voyagers have revealed about the solar system and interstellar space, what happens when their power finally runs out, and whether anyone — or anything — might ever intercept the messages from Earth they carry.
paras.zh: 以下是“旅行者”号探测器揭示的有关太阳系和星际空间的信息，当它们的能量最终耗尽时会发生什么，以及是否有人（或任何东西）可能拦截它们携带的来自地球的信息。

paras.en: How far are Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 from Earth now?
paras.zh: 现在，旅行者1号和旅行者2号距离地球有多远？

paras.en: Voyager 1, cruising through space at nearly 38,000 mph (61,000 km/h), is just shy of 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers) from Earth. That's the distance light travels in 24 hours, also known as one light-day. The spacecraft will reach this milestone on Nov. 18 at 5:16:07 a.m. ET, after traveling through space for 49 years, two months and 11 days.
paras.zh: 旅行者1号正以近38,000英里/小时（61,000公里/小时）的速度在太空中航行，距离地球仅不到160亿英里（约260亿公里）。这是光在24小时内传播的距离，也称为一个光日。这艘太空船在太空中飞行了49年零2个月零11天后，将于美国东部时间11月18日凌晨5:16:07达到这一里程碑。

paras.en: As long as that sounds, "it's still pathetically slow in the grand scheme of things," Lee told Live Science.
paras.zh: 李博士在接受《Live Science》采访时表示，尽管听起来很长，但“从大局来看，这仍然慢得可怜”。

paras.en: Scientifically speaking, Voyager 1 hasn't even left its home neighborhood yet. In 2012, the probe traveled beyond the heliosphere, the bubble of plasma blown outward by the sun that shields the planets from incoming cosmic radiation. But it still remains within the sun's gravitational grasp, which extends past the Oort Cloud — a vast spherical shell of icy bodies surrounding the solar system. Voyager 1 will need about 300 more years just to reach the cloud's inner edge, and possibly 30,000 years to fly beyond it, according to NASA.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: "If anything, it reminds us of the sheer vastness of space and time, and how this spacecraft is just a little mote of dust that's barely drifted out of the solar system still," Lee said.
paras.zh: “如果说有什么意义的话，那就是它提醒我们宇宙空间和时间的浩瀚无边，以及这艘宇宙飞船只是一个微尘，甚至还没有飘出太阳系。”李说。

paras.en: On its current path, Voyager 1 will pass within 1.7 light-years of a dim star called Gliese 445 in about 40,000 years, at which point it will be closer to that star than to our own sun. Farther out, the nearest star system to our own, Proxima Centauri, sits about 4.24 light-years away — more than 1,500 times farther than Voyager 1 will be on Nov. 18.
paras.zh: 按照目前的轨道，旅行者1号将在大约4万年后经过一颗名为格利泽445的暗星，距离其1.7光年以内，届时它将比离我们的太阳更接近那颗恒星。再往外，距离我们最近的恒星系统比邻星（Proxima Centauri）距离我们约4.24光年，比11月18日旅行者1号的距离远1500多倍。

paras.en: Meanwhile Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2, took a different route through the solar system after both probes launched in 1977, in order to swing past Uranus and Neptune after revisiting Jupiter and Saturn. Currently in interstellar space about 13 billion miles (21 million km) from Earth, Voyager 2 will reach its own light-day mark in November 2035, according to NASA.
paras.zh: 与此同时，旅行者1号的姊妹飞船旅行者2号在1977年两艘探测器发射后，选择了不同的路线穿越太阳系，以便在再次飞掠木星和土星后，飞掠天王星和海王星。根据美国宇航局的说法，目前“旅行者2号”正位于距离地球约130亿英里（2100万公里）的星际空间中，它将于2035年11月达到自己的光日里程碑。

paras.en: What does a light-day mean for talking to Voyager 1?
paras.zh: 对于与“旅行者1号”的通信来说，一个光日意味着什么？

paras.en: Crossing the one-light-day mark doesn't change how NASA communicates with the probe, though it does demand more patience.
paras.zh: 虽然跨越一光日大关不会改变NASA与探测器的通信方式，但确实需要更多的耐心。

paras.en: NASA talks to the spacecraft using radio signals, which travel at the speed of light. At a distance of one light-day, a signal sent from Earth takes 24 hours to reach Voyager 1, and a reply takes another 24 hours to make the return journey.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局使用以光速传播的无线电信号与航天器进行通信。在距离一个光日的地方，从地球发出的信号需要 24 小时才能到达“旅行者 1 号”，而回复则需要再花 24 小时才能完成返回的旅程。

paras.en: "If you want to say 'hello' to Voyager, you send your message and then you go home and you wait two days before you finally get a response," Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager at JPL, said in a recent statement.
paras.zh: “如果你想向‘旅行者’号问好，你需要先发送消息，然后回家等待两天，最后才会收到回复。”喷气推进实验室（JPL）的‘旅行者’号项目经理苏珊·多德（Suzanne Dodd）在最近的一份声明中说道。

paras.en: As the spacecraft continues to cruise deeper into space, that wait will grow longer. Moreover, 50 years of traversing the solar system and the increasing distance from our sun takes a toll on the probe itself. Because sunlight in the outer reaches is far too faint for solar panels, Voyager 1 relies on nuclear batteries that convert heat from the natural decay of plutonium into electricity. That supply is gradually dwindling, prompting NASA to gradually shut down nonessential instruments to conserve what energy remains and extend the mission as much as possible.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Kelly Perry, a data systems engineer on the Voyager program at JPL, told Live Science via email that the mission team's priority remains the same: "keep the spacecraft going as long as possible."
paras.zh: 喷气推进实验室（JPL）“旅行者”计划的数据系统工程师凯莉·佩里（Kelly Perry）通过电子邮件告诉《生活科学》杂志，任务团队的优先事项仍然不变：“让航天器尽可能长时间地运行。”

paras.en: Before the Voyagers launched, the outer solar system was largely a blur of telescopic speculation. The twin probes took advantage of a planetary alignment that comes around only once every 176 years, using the gravity of giant planets to slingshot themselves onward.
paras.zh: 在“旅行者”号探测器发射之前，太阳系外围区域在望远镜中大多是一片模糊，只能靠猜测。这对双胞胎探测器利用了176年才出现一次的行星排列，借助巨行星的引力将自己弹射出去。

paras.en: Together, they have discovered 23 moons across the outer solar system, revealed faint rings around Jupiter and captured the first detailed atmospheric profiles of Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. They also gave the first detailed, close-up views of Jupiter's moon Europa, transforming our perception of it from a blurry speck into a remarkably smooth, geologically young world — and now one of the prime candidates for finding extraterrestrial life.
paras.zh: 它们共同发现了太阳系外围的23颗卫星，揭示了木星周围的微弱光环，并首次捕捉到了土星、天王星和海王星的详细大气剖面图。它们还首次提供了木卫二的详细近距离图像，将我们对它的认知从一个模糊的小点转变为一个光滑得令人惊叹、地质上年轻的世界——而现在，它已成为寻找地外生命的主要候选者之一。

paras.en: Among the more striking finds, Voyager 1 spotted active volcanoes on Jupiter's moon Io in 1979, the first time they had been seen on any world other than Earth.
paras.zh: 在更引人注目的发现中，旅行者1号于1979年在木星的卫星木卫一上发现了活火山，这是人类首次在地球以外的星球上看到活火山。

paras.en: "We had no idea what they looked like," Lee said. "And all of a sudden they became places we could map, imagine ourselves exploring, landing on…they became places," he added.
paras.zh: “我们根本不知道它们是什么样子，”李说。“突然之间，它们变成了我们可以绘制地图的地方，我们可以想象自己去探索、降落……它们变成了地方。”他补充道。

paras.en: "That's what Voyager was for me — a voyage of discovery," he said.
paras.zh: “对我来说，这就是‘旅行者’号的意义所在——一次探索之旅。”他说。

paras.en: These discoveries laid the groundwork for decades of follow-up exploration, including NASA's Galileo mission to Jupiter and the Cassini mission to Saturn. Decades later, as the only spacecraft to return in situ data from outside the heliosphere, the probes also proved that interstellar space is a dynamic, complex frontier rather than an empty vacuum.
paras.zh: 这些发现为之后的数十年后续探索奠定了基础，包括美国宇航局的伽利略号木星探测任务和卡西尼号土星探测任务。几十年后，作为唯一一艘从太阳系外返回原位数据的航天器，这两艘探测器还证明了星际空间是一个动态、复杂的疆域，而非空荡荡的真空。

paras.en: How much time does Voyager 1 have left, and what happens when it falls silent?
paras.zh: 旅行者1号还剩下多少时间，它停止工作后会发生什么？

paras.en: Each Voyager spacecraft launched with 10 science instruments. Today, only two remain active on Voyager 1 and three on Voyager 2, measuring the magnetic fields, plasma and cosmic rays of interstellar space.
paras.zh: 每艘“旅行者”号太空船在发射时都搭载了10台科学仪器。如今，旅行者1号上仅有两台仪器仍在运行，旅行者2号上仅有三台仪器仍在运行，它们用于测量星际空间的磁场、等离子体和宇宙射线。

paras.en: NASA began switching off the others one by one decades ago to conserve power, including the camera on Voyager 1 just minutes after it snapped the famous "Pale Blue Dot" portrait of the solar system in 1990. Ongoing power-saving reconfigurations have since helped keep the aging spacecraft operational nearly 50 years into its lifetime.
paras.zh: 几十年前，为了节约能源，美国宇航局开始逐一关闭其他仪器，包括1990年“旅行者1号”拍摄完著名的太阳系“苍白蓝点”照片几分钟后就关闭了其上的摄像头。此后，持续进行的节能重新配置帮助这艘老旧的航天器在服役近50年后仍能保持运行。

paras.en: In one such recent effort, nicknamed the "Big Bang," engineers shut off certain high-power subsystems while switching on lower-power alternatives, which "bought us almost two more years during which we will not need to turn any instrument off," Perry said.
paras.zh: 在最近的一次此类努力中，工程师们关闭了一些大功率子系统，同时开启了低功率替代方案，这一举措被戏称为“大爆炸”。佩里表示：“这为我们争取了将近两年的时间，在这段时间内，我们无需关闭任何仪器。”

paras.en: With onboard power steadily dwindling, however, "there's a recognition that it won't be forever," Deana Weibel, an anthropologist at the Grand Valley State University in Michigan who co-authored an upcoming book about the Golden Record aboard the Voyager probes, told Live Science.
paras.zh: 然而，随着星际探测器上的电力稳步减少，“人们认识到，这不会永远持续下去。”密歇根州大峡谷州立大学的人类学家迪娜·韦贝尔（Deana Weibel）在接受《直播科学》采访时表示。她还与他人合著了一本即将出版的关于“旅行者”号探测器上“黄金唱片”的书。

paras.en: Because Voyager is a science mission, its mission will be considered finished when "no science instruments are operational," Perry said. "The Science Team decided that the last remaining instrument will be the magnetometer," she added. "We will never intentionally power off this instrument."
paras.zh: 佩里表示，由于“旅行者”号是一项科学任务，当“所有科学仪器都无法运行”时，其任务将被视为结束。她补充说：“科学团队决定，最后剩下的仪器将是磁强计。” “我们绝不会故意关闭这台仪器。”

paras.en: After the science data eventually stops, both probes may still keep beaming back basic engineering updates, such as about their health and power status, until around 2036, according to NASA. Even after the spacecraft finally fall silent, they will keep coasting through interstellar space, and "analysis shows that they should remain intact," Perry said.
Scientists will still be able to calculate their positions based on their last known speed and trajectories, Weibel said. "We'll know intellectually where it is unless it gets intercepted."
Could an alien civilization discover the Voyager probes?
Theoretically, yes. But interstellar space is so unfathomably vast that the chances of aliens finding the probes are vanishingly small, Lee said.

That makes it unlikely that aliens will ever find the Voyager Golden Records — twin gold-plated discs meant to portray the diversity of life on Earth. They hold sounds such as wind and animal calls, greetings in 55 languages, images of our planet and a celestial map pinpointing its location — all intended for a hypothetical civilization capable of retrieving and playing them. (The probes also carry visual instructions for spinning the records).
In that sense, the Golden Records are as much an artistic exercise as a scientific one.

"The chances of us going after Voyager 1 and bringing it back for the Smithsonian — not that it's likely — are more believable than any chance of an alien civilization finding it, and then playing the record," Lee said.

If an extraterrestrial civilization did find the probe after we lost contact with it, "we would have no way of knowing," Weibel added. "It becomes something that's powered entirely by imagination at that point."

So why send a message at all? All three scientists interviewed for this story see the Golden Record as a cosmic time capsule, a symbolic gesture meant to unite humanity around a shared home planet. For all its imperfections, including the omission of some widely spoken languages and a few mislabeled tracks, the disc remains an enduring emblem of human presence on Earth, they said.

"Knowing that Voyager will continue its mission long past my lifetime actually gives me comfort," Perry told Live Science. "Although I won't be able to speak to the Voyager spacecraft any more, I love knowing that I'll always be able to look to the stars and know they're still on their way."

Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Space.com, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston. Follow her on BlueSky @skuthunur.bsky.social
